q: How many positive integers n from 1 through 1000 make n^2 + n + 1 divisible by 7?
Among all 8-bit binary strings from 00000000 through 11111111, how many contain exactly one contiguous block of 1s? Zeros may form any number of blocks; exclude the all-zero string.
Five people A, B, C, D, and E sit around a round table. Rotations are identical but reflections are distinct. How many arrangements have A and B nonadjacent?
How many integers from 1 through 50 are abundant, meaning the sum of all proper divisors is greater than the integer itself?

Fill a 3x3 grid with the distinct integers 1 through 9 exactly once so every row, column, and both diagonals sum to 15. Count rotations and reflections as different arrangements. How many arrangements exist?
Two fair six-sided dice are rolled. The product is a perfect square. Write the probability as a reduced fraction a/b and compute a+b.
Use the digits 1 through 9 exactly once to form three ordered three-digit numbers A, B, and C. How many ordered triples satisfy A+B+C=1332?
What is the smallest positive integer n for which n! ends in exactly three consecutive zeros?
How many integer-coordinate points (x,y) satisfy 0<=x<=10, 0<=y<=10, and x+y is prime?
Choose five distinct positive integers whose sum is exactly 20. What is the maximum possible product?
Eight distinct people are divided into two unlabeled teams of four. How many divisions are possible?
Starting at (0,0), move only one unit right or one unit up until reaching (7,5). How many paths must pass through (3,2)?
How many integers from 1 through 100 are divisible by 3 or 5 but not by 15?
How many six-digit positive integers have all digits distinct, odd digits in positions 1,3,5, and even digits in positions 2,4,6? Odd digits are 1,3,5,7,9 and even digits are 0,2,4,6,8.
A regular dodecahedron has 12 faces, 20 vertices, and 30 edges. Compute faces + vertices - edges.

Five people—Minsu, Younghee, Chulsoo, Sujin, and Jaewon—come from distinct cities (Seoul, Busan, Daegu, Incheon, Gwangju) and have distinct jobs (doctor, teacher, farmer, painter, cook). Clues: (1) Minsu is not from Seoul. (2) The doctor is from Busan. (3) Younghee is the teacher and is not from Seoul. (4) The painter is from Incheon, and Jaewon is not the painter. (5) Chulsoo is the cook. (6) Sujin is from Gwangju. (7) Jaewon is not from Daegu. (8) Minsu is not the doctor. What is Jaewon's job?
An item with a list price of 10,000 is discounted by 20%, then the discounted price is increased by 20%. By exactly how much is the final price below the original list price?

Every islander is either a knight who always tells the truth or a liar who always lies. X says, 'Y and Z are the same type.' Y says, 'X and Z are both liars.' Z says, 'X is a knight.' How many of the three are knights?

Machines A, B, and C make 50%, 30%, and 20% of a factory's output. Their defect rates are 2%, 5%, and 1%, respectively. A randomly selected item is defective. What is the probability, as a reduced fraction, that it came from B?
A sequence is defined by a(1)=1, a(2)=2, and a(n)=(a(n-1)*a(n-2)) mod 97 for n>=3. Find a(10).
